CORE and S&OP KPIs

What to measure and why, and how to diagnose a manual process before automating it.

1. CORE methodology

A checklist for any process that lives in a manual Excel today. Walk through it in order and state which phase the process is in.

PhaseQuestionTypical deliverable
C — ControlIs the input data reliable, from a single source, and owned by someone? Does the process serve the business goal?Source inventory, data contract, schema validations, null and duplicate control, quality rules
O — OptimizeWhich manual, repetitive steps can be removed? What logic is redundant?VBA, Power Automate, Python ETL, scheduled extraction; tuned queries and joins
R — RedesignCan the static report become a model and an interactive dashboard?Star schema, DAX measures, cross-filtering dashboard, modular pipelines
E — EvolveDoes it scale? Does it plug into the S&OP cycle?Fabric lakehouse, Parquet or Delta, pipelines, monitoring, alerts, continuous improvement

Rules:

  • C comes first. Do not jump to R or E until C is solved: a dashboard on uncontrolled data only automates chaos.
  • Measurable impact. Every proposal closes with a number: hours per week saved, sources consolidated (for example, 10 to 3), percentage of overproduction reduced, stoppages avoided.
  • Usual tool path: Excel/VBA → Python/Power Automate → Power BI on a star schema → Fabric.
  • Reuse first. Existing models are reused before a new one is created.

2. CTCO structure

When a request is vague, restructure it into these four parts and confirm before starting.

PartContent
ContextEnvironment, scope (work or personal), systems involved
TaskExact technical actions and transformations
ConstraintsCoding, security and data-governance standards
OutputDeliverable format

3. KPIs

For every KPI, always define four things:

  • the formula;
  • the grain (day or week, plant, line, material);
  • the source;
  • what counts as "good".
KPIFormulaNotes
OEEAvailability × Performance × Quality
  • Availability = run time / planned time
  • Performance = (pieces × ideal cycle) / run time
  • Quality = good pieces / total pieces
Schedule AdherenceΣ min(actual, plan) / Σ plan, per line and periodOne day's overproduction must not offset another day's shortfall
Days of coverageAvailable inventory / average daily demandState the demand window: forward-looking or historical
ShortagesNet requirement > available on the need dateShow the first shortage date and the critical material
AgingDays since receipt or last movement, in bucketsTypical buckets: 0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and over 90
FPYGood pieces first time / pieces inCalculated per station; the total yield is the product of all stations
Supply–demand nettingAvailable + open supply − open demand, accumulated by dateSee section 4
Downtime ParetoDowntime minutes per cause, sorted, with cumulative %The 80/20 drives the action
Excess controlScheduled production above demand / scheduled productionRule to mitigate overproduction
Line balancingCycle time and load per cell vs. taktFinds bottleneck cells

Measures that are an extreme (minimum, maximum, first red day) are not validated by a reconciliation of sums. Two rows that cancel out leave the sum intact and move the extreme. Validate the extreme against its own definition, for example Shortage = max(0, −min(Ending inventory)).

4. Oracle context

  • Netting view: the combined list of open supply and open demand per item is the basis for netting.
  • Oracle queries follow the coding standards: no leading comment (ORA-24374) and no trailing ";".

5. Operational analysis

TopicWhat gets checkedWhat gets delivered
Production schedulingConflicts, overloads, missing inputs, lead-time risk, material shortages, capacity constraintsCorrective actions
InventoryOn-hand, open orders, shortages, coverage, earliest feasible dateAlternatives
Inter-plant transfersThey come as two rows with the same document number and different dates. Match them by document number, never by quantityBoth legs removed, not just the negative one
SOPsKey steps, roles, prerequisites, inputs and outputs, exceptionsStructured summary

6. Dashboard portfolio

The work targets these dashboards:

  • production;
  • inventory and shortages;
  • material availability;
  • schedule adherence;
  • OEE and downtime;
  • quality and yield;
  • demand vs. supply;
  • S&OP performance;
  • management KPI cockpit.

Every new proposal is placed somewhere on this list.
